changes: Extended the accepted annual-fundamentals window from FY1990–1997 through FY2002 and rebuilt the historical and added years together from the named current local files. The accepted top/bottom 1% ROA screen is recalculated over the pooled 1990–2002 window.

Added the existing year-dummy pattern for FY1998–2002 while retaining FY1990 as the omitted year and preserving the accepted OLS terms and geographic/industry/year controls. Retained FYEAR and DATADATE through the handoff and counted actual e(sample) observations by FYEAR; the last added contribution is computed from the fit.
limitations: The accepted reconstruction produces only 182 historical Table 4 complete-case observations and 802 pooled observations, versus the paper-reported Table 4 N=16,750. The paper separately reports a broader 19,737-observation ETR pool and does not explain the difference. The extension adds 620 observations but does not close that coverage/sample-selection gap.

The current merged segment file does not expose legacy GAREA or current SGEOCD/SGEOAR controls. As in the accepted construction, the 12 location controls use explicit SNMS name matching and conservative missing/overlap/currency/source-date rules; this remains a best-effort reconstruction and sharply limits the complete-case estimation sample.

The accepted handoff maps current TXFED and TXFO to paper items #63 and #64, but the historic tax-item crosswalk is not independently established. It also uses ln(1+SALE) and ln(1+PI) for USD-million amounts.

The paper does not publish exact SIC boundaries for excluding banks, insurance carriers and utilities; the accepted code uses historical SIC ranges 6000–6099, 6300–6399 and 4900–4999. The paper also does not identify an OLS variance correction or clustering scheme, so ordinary OLS standard errors are retained.

Because the accepted ROA percentile screen is pooled, recalculating its cut points over FY1990–2002 can change historical membership relative to the saved 1990–1997 fit. The pooled comparison therefore reflects both the extension and the stated screen applied to the expanded window.
